mvp_scope.name: Source BlendR Launch MVP
mvp_scope.definition: A single workspace owner can discover and import products and services from vendor websites and PDF catalogs into a Discovery Session, review and import them into a Universal Catalog, search and filter that catalog, swap AI providers via adapter configuration, and use basic business outputs (flyer and quote PDFs) if time permits. Background workers keep the UI responsive. The platform fully operates with zero AI providers configured.
mvp_scope.rationale: Import-to-catalog flow, provider-agnostic AI, background processing, search/filtering, and simple pricing are the core differentiation. Flyer and Quote Builders are should-have and may be trimmed to MVP-minimal or deferred if risk grows. Analytics, memory, sync, integrations, and team features are deferred to future releases.

launch_critical_workflows.name: Website Discovery Import
launch_critical_workflows.rationale: Core differentiator Playwright-driven discovery; without this, the platform has no automated website import.

launch_critical_workflows.name: PDF Catalog Import
launch_critical_workflows.rationale: PDF imports are equal in status to website imports per locked PRD decision.

launch_critical_workflows.name: Discovery Session Review and Import
launch_critical_workflows.rationale: Gates all imports; locked principle; prevents auto-import risk.

launch_critical_workflows.name: Universal Catalog Management
launch_critical_workflows.rationale: Owned catalog is the platform's primary asset.

launch_critical_workflows.name: AI Provider Configuration and Capability Routing
launch_critical_workflows.rationale: Provider-agnostic architecture is locked; required even though AI is optional.

launch_critical_workflows.name: Manual Entry
launch_critical_workflows.rationale: First-class workflow; validates that the platform runs with zero AI providers.

launch_critical_systems.system: Playwright scraping engine with category tree, lazy scraping, parallel jobs, retry/resume per category
Background job queue with idempotent retries
Ingestion and normalization engine producing Source BlendR normalized JSON
AI provider adapter architecture + provider registry + capability router with graceful degradation
Validation Engine gating Discovery Session imports to catalog
Universal Catalog with Universal Catalog Items (products, services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, installation)
Multi-tenant workspace with AI settings and branding
Search index (global, vendor, category, item type, tags, favorites)

phase_1_foundation.name: Foundation
phase_1_foundation.description: Multi-tenant workspace, background queue, vendor records, sync history scaffolding.

phase_2_import_and_ai.name: Import and AI
phase_2_import_and_ai.description: Playwright website discovery, PDF import, AI adapter architecture + provider registry + capability router, Discovery Session staging.

phase_3_catalog_and_pricing.name: Catalog and Pricing
phase_3_catalog_and_pricing.description: Universal Catalog Items, search/filtering/tags/favorites, pricing modes (fixed, percentage, manual).

phase_4_business_outputs.name: Business Outputs (should-have)
phase_4_business_outputs.description: Minimal Flyer Builder and Quote Builder with PDF export. Defer if MVP risk grows.

manual_workaround_candidates.manual_workaround: If no AI providers are configured, all AI-extraction workflows degrade to manual entry. This is the required graceful degradation behavior.
If Document Memory is deferred, users can re-import a PDF and manually compare to the prior catalog using vendor sync history notes.
If Vendor Memory is deferred, users re-run website discovery and manually diff in the Discovery Session.
If Analytics is deferred, users export the catalog and use external tools.
If manual sync is deferred, users re-run discovery manually.

complexity_reductions.reduction: Ship V1 with a single AIProvider interface and one built-in adapter (e.g., OpenAI-compatible) plus Ollama for local. Other adapters can be added post-launch without redesign.
complexity_reductions.tradeoff: Slightly fewer launch providers; acceptable because the adapter contract is stable.

complexity_reductions.reduction: Ship fixed, percentage, and manual only; defer formula pricing.
complexity_reductions.tradeoff: No rule-based prices at launch; manual override is available.

complexity_reductions.reduction: Ship basic collections if budget allows; otherwise defer.
complexity_reductions.tradeoff: Users can group items via tags/manual workaround initially.

complexity_reductions.reduction: Ship vendor spend and catalog growth only; defer the rest.
Ship manual sync only; defer scheduled sync.
Ship minimal MVP-capable versions or defer to phase 4 if MVP risk grows.

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: Build Source BlendR as an AI-agnostic Vendor Intelligence Platform: multi-tenant workspaces, Playwright-first website discovery, PDF catalog extraction, Discovery Session staging before import, Universal Catalog Items (products, services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, installation), AI Provider Adapter Architecture with capability routing, background workers, and deferred future features per the PRD.
alternatives_considered: Single AI provider only (rejected: violates AI-agnostic locked principle)
Auto-import without Discovery Sessions (rejected: violates discovery-before-import locked principle)
Product-only catalog (rejected: violates Universal Catalog Items locked decision)
Plug-in marketplace architecture (rejected: explicitly out of scope in Inference Layer summary)
key_decisions: Playwright is the locked web discovery engine
AI is provider-agnostic via adapter architecture and capability router
Discovery Sessions always gate catalog imports
Universal Catalog Items replace Product-only schema
Manual entry is a first-class workflow; platform runs with zero AI providers
Background workers handle scraping and AI processing
PDF imports are equal in status to website imports
Flyer and Quote Builders are should-have; may be trimmed or deferred to protect MVP risk

assumptions.assumption: Playwright + AI-assisted site analysis handles the majority of target-market vendor sites.
Target users value provider independence and owned catalog data.
Discovery Sessions are accepted as friction-positive vs auto-import competitors.
Universal Catalog Items cover the target market without forcing partial re-architecture.
Background workers keep the UI responsive for expected scrape/AI durations without a streaming UI.

risks.description: Playwright reliability across diverse vendor sites
Target market too small or unwilling to pay

downstream_impact: Stage 2 must validate differentiation hypotheses, market demand, and technical assumptions (Playwright reliability, OCR/AI extraction quality, Universal Catalog schema coverage).
Stage 3 must lock adapter interface, capability router contract, validation engine contract, multi-tenancy isolation boundary, and queue/timeout strategy.
Stage 4 must validate Discovery Session UX and catalog browsing UX.
Stage 5 slices import-to-catalog flow, adapter architecture, and catalog as launch-critical; flyer/quote as should-have.
Stage 6 acceptance criteria must include AI extraction-quality tests per capability and validation engine tests.
